audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 were marked Shen in both layers while whys[1] and whys[2] say the opposite in words ('stays even', 'skill-decided — no clear favourite').
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill for all five lane rows and Shen only from first item on, which matches a 49.18% win rate over 1,346 games. Shen has no kill threat on a champion who dashes in on a 10s Aureate Rush and heals off both Q and R.
audit.corrected: phases[1]/win[1] and phases[2]/win[2] set to Skill; the lane is five even rows, then Shen from the first item. The Shen rows at 5 and 6 stand.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's own defect line says it: NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. Every reference was to a generic 'Ultimate', with no ability named and no number given.
audit.why: Grim Deliverance (R) is 110/95/80 and heals him for a portion of the damage it deals; The Darkin Glaive (Q) is 10s at rank 1; Aureate Rush (E) is 10s; his stab-and-pull W is 14s. Shen's own Shadow Dash is 18s at rank 1, so his engage tools come back roughly twice per one of yours — that is the real reason the lane is even, and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: 110s Grim Deliverance and the 10s Aureate Rush written into tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and early, giving the matchup its first concrete 'wait for X before you Y'.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Zaahen ability was ever named, his healing was attributed to the wrong source ('Extended duels his passive heals through'), and his passive revive was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: His passive is Determination — attacks and abilities on champions stack bonus AD, and at full stacks he gains increased AD AND can revive. The healing comes from The Darkin Glaive (Q) and Grim Deliverance (R), not the passive. Aureate Rush (E) deals percent-health damage, so stacking raw armour is the wrong answer against him. Both interactions are flagged in _missing/shen.json and neither reached the page.
audit.corrected: Q and R named as the heal sources (Grievous Wounds is what decides the long trade), the Glaive recast knock-up written into whys[2] as the reason to taunt after it rather than into it, and the full-Determination revive written into late so a player does not spend the taunt on a corpse that stands back up.

edits.before: The entire laning phase is a genuine skill stage: both of you farm and poke with no kill pressure, and Ki Barrier offsets his empowered Q auto so neither side pulls ahead. Play the straight Q-for-Q trades, keep the wave healthy, and treat every even minute as a win — your spikes come later.
edits.after: The entire laning phase is a genuine skill stage: both of you farm and poke with no kill pressure, and Ki Barrier offsets The Darkin Glaive's double slash so neither side pulls ahead. Aureate Rush (10s) is how he arrives — taunt after that dash, keep the wave healthy, and treat every even minute as a win.

edits.before: With two-plus items you are simply the more impactful champion: the taunt starts fights, R shields save carries, and your durability outlasts his sustain. Splitpush with teleport-ult threat, taunt his engage in teamfights, and let him win a sidelane duel that no longer decides anything.
edits.after: With two-plus items you are simply the more impactful champion: the taunt starts fights, R shields save carries, and your durability outlasts his sustain. Splitpush with teleport-ult threat, and never empty your kit on the kill — at full Determination he revives, so hold the taunt for after he stands up.

notes: Zaahen's W and passive have no names in any file I was given — packet.enemyAbilities is null and _missing/shen.json only supplies The Darkin Glaive (Q), Aureate Rush (E) and Grim Deliverance (R). I referred to the W by effect ('stab-and-pull') rather than invent a name, and to the passive as Determination, which is the stack name Riot's own text uses. Unverified and deliberately NOT written: the revive's cooldown or conditions, whether Shen's taunt holds him through the Glaive recast knock-up, and whether Aureate Rush can be taunt-interrupted mid-dash.
